title: Procedural and substantive democracy
competency: Explain the difference between procedural and substantive democracy.

keywords.def: A view of democracy that focuses on how decisions are made: the process, such as free and regular elections.
A view of democracy that focuses on what a government actually does: the results of its decisions.
The decision with the most votes is accepted.

en.text: Procedural democracy looks at how the people govern themselves. Its principles are universal participation, political equality and majority rule. Voters choose representatives in free elections, and every election procedure is followed. Regular elections in Ethiopia show procedural democracy.

screens.title: Election day
screens.ask: A country holds an election on time, and every voter gets one ballot. What does this show?
screens.after: It shows a fair process. Democracy viewed as a process is called procedural democracy.

screens.title: Two approaches
paras: There are two approaches to understand democracy: procedural and substantive.
The procedural viewpoint stresses the form and process of government.
It asks how the people govern themselves.

screens.title: Procedural democracy
paras: Its principles are universal participation, political equality and majority rule.
Voters choose representatives in free elections.
The electoral process gives elected officials their authority.
In Ethiopia elections are held regularly. This is procedural democracy.
screens.note: REMEMBER: Procedural democracy focuses on how government decisions are made (process).

screens.title: Key words
defs: A view of democracy that focuses on how decisions are made: the process, such as free and regular elections.
The decision with the most votes is accepted.

screens.text: Tap the principles of procedural democracy.
screens.why: The book names these three principles.
screens.clue: Which ones describe a fair process?

screens.text: If all adults can vote, the country is automatically a substantive democracy.
screens.why: Voting alone is not enough. The election should also bring real changes for the people.
screens.clue: What else must elections lead to?

screens.text: Selam's class votes, but the teacher later ignores the result. Which part of democracy is missing?
opts: The result: the decision is not carried out
The process: there was no vote
screens.ans: The result: the decision is not carried out
screens.why: The process (a vote) happened, but the outcome did not follow. That is the substantive side.
screens.clue: Did the vote happen? Did the result happen?

en.text: Substantive democracy looks at what a government actually does. Its policies should match democratic ideals, and the people should have a real say. A state should not only be set up as a democracy, but also function as one. It is also called functional democracy.

screens.title: Same elections, different results
screens.ask: Two countries both hold free elections. In one, life improves for the people. In the other, nothing changes. Which is more democratic in practice?
screens.after: Democracy is also judged by results. This view is called substantive democracy.

screens.title: Substantive democracy
paras: The substantive viewpoint focuses on what a government actually does.
Its policies should be consistent with democratic ideals.
The general population has a real say in how the state runs its affairs.

screens.title: Functional democracy
paras: The state is not only set up as a democracy. It also functions as one.
This type is also called functional democracy.
In Ethiopia, elections should lead to political equality and economic prosperity.
screens.note: REMEMBER: Substantive democracy focuses on the results (outcomes) of government's decisions.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A view of democracy that focuses on what a government actually does: the results of its decisions.

screens.text: The substantive view of democracy focuses on what a government actually does.

screens.title: Process or result?
screens.why: Procedural = how decisions are made. Substantive = what results they bring.
screens.clue: Is it about the way, or the result?

screens.ask: Substantive democracy is also known as ___ democracy.
screens.why: The book calls it functional democracy.
screens.clue: The state must not only be set up as a democracy, but ___ as one.

screens.text: Which question would a substantive view of democracy ask about a new law?
opts: Did it actually improve people's lives?
screens.ans: Did it actually improve people's lives?
screens.why: The substantive view looks at outcomes. The other two are about procedure.

test.text: Which view of democracy focuses on the process of making decisions?
Which view focuses on what a government actually does?
Regular elections are a manifestation of procedural democracy.
test.why: The electoral process is a fundamental part of procedural democracy.

test.ask: Substantive democracy is also called ___ democracy.

test.text: Elections are held on time, but the people's lives never change. What is weak?
test.why: The process works but the outcomes do not.

notes.text: p.77 prints "substantive democracy … serves the interests of those who govern"; this contradicts the rest of the paragraph. It should read "those who are governed". The printed wording is not taught.
p.76 says procedural democracy gives citizens "less influence than in traditional liberal democracies"; unclear claim, not used in items.
